summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman was admitted after a mechanical fall at home, during which she struck her head but denied loss of consciousness. She had a scalp laceration repaired with staples, and imaging showed no acute intracranial or cervical spine injury. Admission labs revealed elevated creatinine and hypokalemia, prompting adjustment of her metolazone dose from three to two times per week. A chest X-ray showed atelectasis without signs of infection, and asymptomatic pyuria was noted but not treated. She remained stable, with no cardiac or neurologic complications, and was discharged home with follow-up in the heart failure clinic and instructions for staple removal and BMP monitoring.
